description: How a warehouse's semantic models become names an agent can call. Every source's models feed one registry of members: each model's dimensions and metrics, and the facts labelled as filters. A member answers to its bare name, to `parent.name`, and to either qualified by its model as `MODEL::name` or `MODEL::parent.name`; the last of these is its key. An error is pinned by the names its message must mention, since the wording belongs to each language. Its `error` field names the kind of failure for a reader, and neither suite asserts it.

models.description: The models every case below reads, all on the source `warehouse`, with the governed data-dict definitions on the same source. Members not given a parent belong to no logical table. `parameters` are a model's typed parameters, and `stubs` are models listed on the same source but not yet read. `context` is a model's first-touch and retrieval prose. `calculations` are a model's verified queries.

values.label: REVENUE
context: Use booked revenue for finance questions.

calculations.name: revenue_by_region
calculations.description: What is booked revenue in each region?
calculations.sql: SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS revenue FROM orders GROUP BY region

calculations.name: order_total
calculations.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders

calculations.name: revenue_by_region
calculations.sql: SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS revenue FROM ledger GROUP BY region

registry.description: The members the registry lists for those models, in order: per model, its dimensions, then its metrics, then the facts labelled as filters. Named filters and other facts are context only and are not listed. `synonyms` is the member's synonyms joined by spaces.

resolution.description: Resolving names against the registry as one kind of member. `filter` resolves only the members labelled as filters. Braces around a name, as the SQL token syntax writes it, are ignored. `expected` is the keys resolved, in order, or an error: `ambiguous` when more than one member of the kind answers to the name, `wrong_kind` when members answer to it but none of the kind, and `missing` when none does.

metric_origin.description: Which pool a metric name belongs to when data-dict metric definitions and native semantic metrics share a source. A definition answers to `name` or `table::name`. A name both pools answer to is ambiguous, and must be qualified. When the source lists models it has not read, a refused name also names them, at most ten with a count of the rest, since only a `MODEL::metric` name reaches their metrics; a name that matches nothing then says no metrics are known yet rather than that none are defined. A case's `unread` replaces the unread labels, which are otherwise the `stubs`, and `empty` leaves out the definitions and the read models. A label is shown as written, whatever characters it holds. An error's `omits` lists text the message must not contain.

mentions: No metrics are known until a listed semantic model is read

pool_text.description: What search_pool returns when the pool holds only these models, the stubs beside them, and no measures or definitions. Members and stubs are ranked with the pool's lexical ranking: a member by its name, model, kind, label, description, and synonyms, a stub by its name, label, backend, and description, and a verified query by its key, name, and description. A member is written by its bare name when that is unambiguous and by its key otherwise. `source_names` are the sources an agent with several names; a member on one of them says so. `empty` is the reply for a pool with nothing in it.

call_metrics.description: Calls over native metrics that are refused before any SQL runs, on the source holding these models and definitions. A call draws its metrics from data-dict definitions or from one native semantic model, never both and never two models, resolves its dimensions within that model, and binds `arguments` only to that model's declared parameters. `arguments` is the JSON text the model writes. Each pinned phrase must appear in the error.

cases.name: metrics from both pools in one call are refused

mentions: Metrics in one call must come from either data-dict definitions or one native semantic model.

cases.name: native metrics from two models in one call are refused

mentions: Metrics in one call must belong to one native semantic model.

cases.name: arguments are refused for data-dict metrics

mentions: `arguments` is supported only for native semantic metrics.

cases.name: a required parameter must be given
an argument the model does not declare is refused
an argument of the wrong type is refused
a dimension resolves within the metrics' model

mentions: No native semantic dimension is named
`metrics` must contain at least one metric name.

description_text.description: What describe_table returns for a semantic model: its name and description, every public member qualified by the model with its kind and detail, the parameters call_metrics binds, its verified queries, and the model's context prose. A member's detail is its description, or its label when it has none. `error` is the reason a listed model's definition could not be read, which is described in place of its members.

first_touch.description: The semantic-model prose a table's first touch adds: the first-touch context of every model that reads the table, de-duplicated in model order. A model reads a table when one of its dependencies is the relation's warehouse identity, or its id when it has none, compared exactly, so a Snowflake name differing only in case is another table. A label that names no relation gets nothing.

calculations.description: The verified queries the models offer, as call_calculation finds them. A query's key is its model's label and its name joined by `::`. A query answers to its name or its key among the queries on the source the call names, and a name more than one query answers to must be given as a key.
